mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically from -9.1% to -3.4% over four weeks, indicating a consistent recovery trend. This momentum will persist over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC further positive as the baseline effect compounds.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 5.7 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below the mean of the last 28 days, or the week-on-week improvement rate reverses for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has risen from 2.3% to 5.7% over four weeks, signaling increased essential-goods shopping trips. Consumers making frequent grocery visits will incidentally increase retail-and-recreation visits in co-located shopping districts, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at 5.7% in t-0w, highest in snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above 5.0%, or GROCERY_PHARM declines below 4.0% in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has stabilized at -27.7% after declining from -31.9%, indicating public-transport restrictions are no longer tightening. This stabilization signals policy relaxation, which will permit retail-and-recreation venues to operate with fewer capacity constraints, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change is less than 1 percentage point for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 4.2 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w, then stabilized
failure_condition: TRANSIT declines by more than 2 percentage points in the next week, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined sharply to -16.4% in t-0w, indicating outdoor recreation is suppressed by seasonal weather or policy. This suppression will redirect leisure activity indoors to retail-and-recreation venues, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks as consumers substitute outdoor for indoor activities.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -15.0% for one week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -16.4% in t-0w, lowest in snapshot
failure_condition: PARKS mobility recovers above -10.0% within two weeks without a corresponding increase in RETAIL_REC, or RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has remained stable at -6.7% for two consecutive weeks, indicating workplace attendance has plateaued. This plateau signals that remote-work arrangements are locked in, reducing commuter-driven retail visits and suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week change is less than 0.5 percentage points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES unchanged at -6.7% from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises by more than 2 percentage points in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28 days by more than 3 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 4.0% to 3.1% over four weeks, indicating residents are spending less time at home. This outbound shift, combined with rising GROCERY_PHARM, signals consumers are increasingly mobile and will sustain higher RETAIL_REC visits over the next four weeks as confidence in public spaces grows.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines below 3.5% AND GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 5.0% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declining trend over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rises above 4.0% in the next week, or RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days fails to exceed the prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both suppressed (-27.7% and -6.7% respectively), indicating coordinated restrictions on commuting and public transport. If these restrictions remain in place for the next four weeks without further tightening, RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed as commuter-driven retail demand stays low.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -25.0% AND WORKPLACES remains below -5.0% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:Both series remain deeply suppressed in t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -20.0% or WORKPLACES rises above -4.0% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC improvement rate has decelerated from 2.2 percentage points (t-3w to t-2w) to 1.7 percentage points (t-1w to t-0w), indicating the recovery is losing momentum. This deceleration will continue over the next four weeks as the easiest gains have been captured, resulting in lower RETAIL_REC growth or stagnation.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC week-on-week improvement falls below 1.5 percentage points for one week
evidence_refs: fact:Week-on-week improvement rate declining from 2.2 to 1.7 percentage points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC week-on-week improvement accelerates to above 2.0 percentage points, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28 days by more than 2 percentage points.
